 37s ago 16.30 EST 79 min Spain are getting Lamine on the ball now and he teases Hall, who does really well not to buy what’s being sold, eventually blocking his man off with help from Trafford, and England clear.
 Share 2m ago 16.29 EST 78 min There’s such tempo and intensity to this game, and Tuchel acts, taking off Kane and introducing Lewis-Skelly. I can see why he’s done that but, on this occasion, I might’ve kept Kane on as a target man to hold the ball; who is the striker now?
 Share 3m ago 16.27 EST 77 min A bit of England possession, Gordon and Bellingham doing well in the inside-left channel, but this time when Bellingham crosses the ball soars behind for a goalkick.
 Share 4m ago 16.26 EST GOAL! Spain 2-3 England (Williams 75)
 How will England eff it up? Like this. Gordon tarries in possession, Pedri robbing him, then a fantastic first-time pass from Fermin sends Lamine away down the left. His low cross is a delight, Williams arriving on to it without breaking stride, and he swishes a finish in off the near post. It’s a different game now!
 Share 6m ago 16.25 EST 73 min Spain win a corner down the right which yields another from the left. This time it goes short and, when the ball is clipped to the far post, Belling ham opts to let it go but Oyarzabal is behind him, and when he forces the cut-back, Fermin shoots … and Trafford parries. Pressure is building…
 Share 8m ago 16.22 EST 72 min A further change for Spain , Williams replacing Zubimendi as De la Fuente goes for it.
 Share 9m ago 16.21 EST 70 min Spain find Lamine on the right side of the box, but his attempted curler is blocked at source. England have defended superbly so far, the penalty Spain’s first shot on target.
 Share 10m ago 16.20 EST 69 min This is a proper test for England; not one Tuchel will have wanted but perhaps one the team needs. If they can make it through this, so wind up dominating Spain with 11, then seeing them away with 10, they’ll end the evening a different side to the one which started it. Lose and – though it’ll hurt – they can blame individual error.
 Share Updated at  16.21 EST 12m ago 16.18 EST 67 min Someone on the England bench is booked, and I wonder if Tuchel contemplates a change. He needs keep an out-ball, but perhaps midfield control means he remove Rogers for, perhaps, Lewis-Skelly.
 Share 14m ago 16.16 EST GOAL! Spain 1-3 England (Oyarzabal pen 65)
 Oyarzabal ambles up, skips, and when Trafford dives left, he sweeps right. Hold on to your toupees, this is going to be a serious 25 minutes.
 View image in fullscreen Mikel Oyarzabal of Spain celebrates scoring. Photograph: David Ramos/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.20 EST 15m ago 16.15 EST PENALTY TO SPAIN AND A RED CARD FOR ELLIOT ANDERSON!
 64 min That question, eh? How will England eff it up? Like thus: Quansah is mugged by Lamine, the first time England have been so caught, and when Baena sweeps him in, Anderson hauls him back, a rash call, and Spain have a route back into the game!
 View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal of Spain is fouled in the penalty area by Elliot Anderson of England which resulted in a red card for Anderson. Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.20 EST 17m ago 16.13 EST 62 min “Are you Scotland in disguise?” sing the away end, a disbelieving Philip Cornwall back in touch BUT EXCUSE ME WHILE I INTERRUPT MYSELF ONCE MORE!
 Share 19m ago 16.12 EST 61 min Gordon, who’s having a fine night, win another corner, and England will fancy another here, but this time Rice’s floaty delivery is easily fielded by Simon.
 Share 19m ago 16.11 EST 60 min And what a moment of redemption that is for White. Jeered by his own fans after leaving the World Cp squad in 2022, he’s nicely reintegrated now, and that was the kind of finish you’d expect to see from Pedro Porro. That is some serious praise.
 Share 21m ago 16.09 EST GOAL! Spain 0-3 England (White 58)
 Kane across the face of the box to Bellingham, who caresses in behind for White! He takes a touch, narrowing the angle but forcing the keeper to move then, when Simon spreads himself, he picks a very deliberate finish through the keeper’s legs! This is a hiding!
 View image in fullscreen England's Ben White scores their side's third goal. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at  16.10 EST 23m ago 16.08 EST 57 min Spain haven’t lost for 43 games …and BUT EXCUSE ME WHILE I INTERRUPT MYSELF … THEY’RE GOING TO LOSE TONIGHT!
 Share 23m ago 16.07 EST 56 min Bellingham, whose good work won the corner from which England scored, wins another ion similar style, this time down the left, as we see footgge of the England goal, Tuchel on the touchline also applying brow to imaginary ball – that’s how much time and space Konsa had. This time, the corner comes to nowt.
 Share 25m ago 16.06 EST 54 min Minor Spain protests for a free-kick of some sort, but VAR isn’t interested. Konsa couldn’t have been freer, the question on everybody’s lips a familiar one: how will they eff it up from here?
 Share 26m ago 16.04 EST GOAL! Spain 0-2 England (Konsa 53)
 A Rice outswinger and, in the middle of the box, Konsa has maybe five yards of space all around him to run in and guide home from seven yards. England are all over this!
 View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa of England scores his team’s second goal. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Konsa celebrates scoring his team’s second goal. Photograph: Michael Regan/The FA/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.05 EST 27m ago 16.03 EST 52 min Zubimendi picks up a poor pass and punches between Anderosn and Rice, finding Lamine … whose trivela cross is straight at Trafford. Then England find Bellingham down the right of the box and he delays well before winning a corner off Pedri, gesticulating to where he thinks the away end is, but isn’t.
 Share 29m ago 16.01 EST 51 min Down the right, 30 yards from goal, Rice will swing the free-kick out … and Huijsen heads away well, facing his own goal.
 Share 30m ago 16.00 EST 49 min Lamine spreads wide to Cucurella, then Spain work it back to him, Hall delaying before Gordon confiscates possession. Those two have been brilliant so far and, when England counter, Rogers cuts inside Cucurella, who trips him and is booked.
 Share 31m ago 15.59 EST 48 min England win it high and win a throw, Tuchel’s alacrity in returning the ball evidencing their intent to speed up the game and impose their will. Spain soon have possession back, but it’s a message not to retreat.
 Share 33m ago 15.58 EST 48 min Already, Spain look calmer, Pedri linking play and finding pockets. England will, as Tuchel warned, have to be patient.
 Share 34m ago 15.56 EST 47 min “As I’m sure 347 other people are also pointing out,” chortles Bob O’Hara, “Pochettino made a pretty big managerial eff-up this week.”
 I fear that lush mane is on borrowed time – on which point is it just me who sees Stan Rizzo from Mad Men?
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: PR Company Handout Share 34m ago 15.56 EST 46 min We go again, those Spain changes reflecting England’s superiority.
 Share 35m ago 15.55 EST A triple Spain change: Huijsen, Pedri and Fermin on; Ruiz, Cubarsi and Merino off.
 Share 37m ago 15.54 EST Back come our teams… 
 Share 38m ago 15.53 EST Elsewhere, France are level at 0-0 playing Turkey in Bordeaux; Belgium have come from 1-0 down to lead Italy 3-1. As it stands, it’ll be France and Belgium moving on, Italy’s renaissance curtailed.
 Share 39m ago 15.52 EST “Benitez, Robbie Fowler’s last game for Liverpool,” writes Paul Oakes . “Takes him off with five minutes to go. Liverpool get a penalty one minute later.”
 I guess the idea was right, though – a proper reception.
 Share 41m ago 15.50 EST “What did Ferguson do against Chelsea in 2010?” asks Joshua Keeling. In a game United needed to not lose, he picked Nevlle, Giggs and Scholes, though younger, harder-running players had excelled against Bayern the previous midweek, United lost the game, lost the title, and lost the chance of four in a row.
 Share 45m ago 15.46 EST I wonder if De la Fuente will move to Pedri; the control we expect from Spain isn’t there tonight, and his ability to tempo-set might change this game. So far, Merino has been a cone, and it’s no great surprise; he’s a late-doors player, one who finds a goal when you’re desperate for one, rather than someone who gets involved in general play.
